question:
(i) Explain why a material with high retentivity and high coercivity is suitable for making a permanent magnet.
(ii) Why is the same material not suitable for making the core of an electromagnet?

options.A:
(i) High retentivity and high coercivity make a material suitable for a permanent magnet because it loses magnetisation easily.
(ii) The same material is ideal for an electromagnet core because it remains magnetised after current is switched off.
options.B:
(i) High retentivity enables the material to retain a large magnetisation, and high coercivity makes it resist demagnetisation; hence it is suitable for a permanent magnet.
(ii) An electromagnet core should magnetise and demagnetise readily, requiring high permeability and low retentivity/coercivity. Therefore, the same material is unsuitable for an electromagnet core.
options.C:
(i) A permanent magnet needs low retentivity and low coercivity so that it can be magnetised repeatedly.
(ii) The same material is unsuitable for an electromagnet because it is too soft.
options.D:
(i) A material with high coercivity has no magnetic moment and therefore cannot be used as a permanent magnet.
(ii) It is unsuitable for an electromagnet only because it has low electrical conductivity.
